One in three American high school graduates do not continue on to college, even though (a) the majority of fastest growing jobs require a postsecondary degree and (b) college graduates earn an average of a million dollars more over the course of their lifetimes. While the college admission landscape is increasingly selective, it also includes a wide range of institutions with varying academic programs, financial aid, and admission rates. These institutions can and do accommodate college students from all different contexts and levels of academic preparation. But many pre-college students do not know how to research colleges, and for those that do, the volume of information needed in order to find, choose, apply to, and pay for the college that fits them best is debilitating. As a result, even high achieving students undermatch or choose not continue on to pursue a postsecondary degree. (Hoxby, 2012) 

CollegePath is a blended learning tool for classrooms that aims to address the duality of this challenge: students need to learn the vocabulary and concepts of the college search process in order to be successful, but they also need confidence in their ability to be successful in the college process in order to be successful. Using Albert Bandura’s self efficacy theory (1977) and the research of Catherine Chase et al. regarding the power of teachable agents (2007), CollegePath employs a diverse collection of short, narrative videos to teach students about the process with very little effort on the part of the instructor. Each video features the story of a person who has gone through the college application process successfully, and is combined with research and reflection activities and transformed into a complete learning module. The modules are designed for the entire classroom to engage with and reflect on the material. In empowering students to become researchers and teachers on the college process, they learn the content and gain the confidence to be successful on their own college paths. 

The following report details the learning theory, design process, and testing results of the preliminary CollegePath demo module, which introduces learners to the concepts of need-based and merit-based financial aid.
